news.title: Transfer news: PSG sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona for about £43m
news.lede: Torres scored Spain's winner against Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final. Ferran Torres, who scored the winning goal for Spain at the World Cup, has joined European champions Paris St-Germain from Barcelona. The 26-year-old has signed a deal with the French champions until 2031 for a reported fee of about 50m euros (£42.7m). He scored the extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second men's World Cup last month, while his stock had already risen considerably after a strong season with Barcelona.

news.title: Why Michaely Bihina is the keeper making waves at Wafcon
news.lede: Michaely Bihina has kept three clean sheets in five matches at Wafcon 2026. One name has become the toast of Cameroon following her heroics at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). Some in the Central African nation are already calling for a statue to built in honour of Michaely Bihina after her incredible performances which have helped the Indomitable Lionesses return to the final for the first time since 2016. The young goalkeeper has been one of the stars of the tournament with player-of-the-match performances against Nigeria in the quarter-finals and hosts Morocco in the last four.

news.title: Call to increase funding for refugee football - and boost Scotland's World Cup hopes
news.lede: The Refugee World Cup Scotland which is staged at the Toryglen Regional Football Centre on the South Side of Glasgow every summer has grown hugely and diversified greatly during the 14 years it has been running. Just eight five-a-side teams took part when the tournament – which was set up by Abdul Bostani, the managing director of the charity Glasgow Afghan United, in 2012 - was first held. But back in June there were no fewer than 24 seven-a-side teams, four of which were comprised entirely of women for the first time ever, involved. In total, over 250 people from more than 50 different countries were in attendance.

news.title: Ghana clear major hurdle in bid to end 20-year World Cup absence
news.lede: Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens. Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens, showed great courage to come from behind and defeat Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 in Casablanca. This victory keeps their dream of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup alive. The match started badly for Ghana.
